title: Hypertension: diagnosis and outpatient management
subject: cardiology
summary: Confirm raised office BP with home or ambulatory readings, assess cardiovascular risk and organ damage, start lifestyle measures, begin most patients with confirmed hypertension on a two-drug single-pill combination (RAS blocker with a calcium channel blocker or thiazide-like diuretic), and aim for SBP 120 to 129 mmHg if tolerated.

sections.title: Measure and diagnose
items: Measure correctly: seated after 5 minutes of rest, back supported, arm at heart level, correct cuff size, validated device; take 2 to 3 readings 1 to 2 minutes apart and average; measure both arms at the first visit and use the higher arm.

ESC 2024 categories (office): non-elevated below 120/70, elevated 120 to 139/70 to 89, hypertension 140/90 mmHg or more. AHA/ACC 2025 labels 130 to 139/80 to 89 as stage 1 and 140/90 or more as stage 2 hypertension.
Confirm with out-of-office BP whenever feasible: home BP average 135/85 or more, daytime ambulatory 135/85 or more, 24-hour ambulatory 130/80 or more, or night-time 120/70 mmHg or more.
Look for white-coat hypertension (high office, normal home) and masked hypertension (normal office, high home). Check standing BP in the elderly, people with diabetes and those with dizziness.

sections.title: Baseline assessment
items: Bloods: sodium, potassium, creatinine and eGFR, fasting glucose or HbA1c, lipid profile; urine dipstick and urine albumin-creatinine ratio; 12-lead ECG (LVH, AF). Echocardiography if the ECG is abnormal or symptoms suggest heart disease.
Estimate 10-year cardiovascular risk (ESC SCORE2 or SCORE2-OP; AHA PREVENT) unless already high risk because of established CVD, diabetes, CKD, familial hypercholesterolaemia or organ damage.

Screen for secondary causes when hypertension is young-onset (under 40), severe, resistant, of sudden onset, or with hypokalaemia: primary aldosteronism (aldosterone-renin ratio), renal disease, renal artery stenosis, sleep apnoea, thyroid disease, drugs (NSAIDs, steroids, oral contraceptives).

sections.title: Lifestyle for everyone
items: Salt below 5 g/day (about 2 g sodium); potassium-enriched salt substitutes help unless CKD or potassium-sparing drugs. Diet rich in vegetables, fruit, pulses and low-fat dairy.
At least 150 minutes/week of moderate aerobic exercise plus resistance training; weight loss if overweight; stop smoking and tobacco chewing; limit alcohol (preferably none).

Elevated BP (120 to 139/70 to 89 mmHg): lifestyle for 3 months, then add drug treatment if BP stays 130/80 mmHg or more and cardiovascular risk is high (10-year risk 10% or more, or diabetes, CKD, established CVD or organ damage).

sections.title: Drug treatment and targets
items: Start drugs promptly for confirmed hypertension (140/90 mmHg or more). Most patients: a two-drug combination, preferably as a single pill: ACE inhibitor or ARB with a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker or a thiazide-like diuretic.
Monotherapy is reasonable for elevated BP with high risk, age 85 or older, moderate to severe frailty, or symptomatic orthostatic hypotension.

Step 2: three-drug combination (RAS blocker plus calcium channel blocker plus thiazide-like diuretic). Step 3 (resistant hypertension): add spironolactone 25 to 50 mg daily (eplerenone if intolerant), then a beta-blocker or alpha-blocker.
Target: ESC 2024 SBP 120 to 129 mmHg and DBP 70 to 79 mmHg in most treated adults if tolerated; AHA/ACC 2025 below 130/80 mmHg. Use as low as reasonably achievable in the very elderly or frail.
Beta-blockers are used for specific indications (angina, post-MI, HFrEF, rate control of AF, pregnancy planning) rather than routine first line.

India (IHCI public programme protocol): start amlodipine 5 mg once daily, then step up at monthly reviews by adding telmisartan 40 mg then 80 mg, increasing amlodipine to 10 mg and adding chlorthalidone (6.25 to 25 mg); the order of steps varies by state.

sections.title: Follow-up
items: Review monthly after starting or changing treatment until controlled (aim within 3 months), then every 3 to 12 months. Encourage home BP monitoring.
Check creatinine and potassium within 2 to 4 weeks of starting or increasing an ACE inhibitor, ARB, diuretic or spironolactone.
Most uncontrolled hypertension is from non-adherence or inadequate doses: use single-pill combinations, once-daily dosing and check adherence before adding drugs.

sections.title: Compelling indications and special groups
items: Diabetes or CKD with albuminuria: ACE inhibitor or ARB (maximum tolerated dose); add SGLT2 inhibitor for kidney protection per diabetes and CKD protocols.
Coronary disease or HFrEF: beta-blocker plus ACE inhibitor or ARB (ARNI in HFrEF); avoid non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers in HFrEF.
Pregnancy or planning pregnancy: stop ACE inhibitors, ARBs, spironolactone and statins; use labetalol, nifedipine modified release or methyldopa.
Previous stroke or TIA: treat to the same target once stable; avoid hypotension in bilateral carotid stenosis.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Diagnosing hypertension on a single office reading.
Combining an ACE inhibitor with an ARB (no benefit, more hyperkalaemia and AKI).
Missing primary aldosteronism in resistant or hypokalaemic hypertension.
Leaving patients on monotherapy at low doses for months (therapeutic inertia).

drugs.name: Amlodipine
drugs.dose: 5 mg orally once daily, increase to 10 mg once daily
drugs.notes: Ankle oedema is dose-related. First step in the IHCI protocol.

drugs.name: Telmisartan
drugs.dose: 40 mg orally once daily, increase to 80 mg once daily
drugs.notes: Check potassium and creatinine. Contraindicated in pregnancy.

drugs.name: Losartan
drugs.dose: 50 mg orally once daily, up to 100 mg daily

drugs.name: Ramipril or enalapril
drugs.dose: Ramipril 2.5 mg once daily, up to 10 mg daily; enalapril 5 mg once daily, up to 40 mg daily in 1 or 2 doses
drugs.notes: Dry cough: switch to an ARB. Angioedema risk. Contraindicated in pregnancy.

drugs.name: Chlorthalidone
drugs.dose: 12.5 mg orally once daily, up to 25 mg daily

drugs.name: Indapamide
drugs.dose: 1.5 mg modified release (or 2.5 mg) orally once daily

drugs.name: Spironolactone
drugs.dose: 25 mg orally once daily, up to 50 mg daily
drugs.notes: Resistant hypertension. Avoid if potassium above 4.5 to 5.0 mmol/L or eGFR below 30 to 45; monitor potassium.

drugs.name: Metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol
drugs.dose: Metoprolol succinate 25 to 100 mg once daily; bisoprolol 2.5 to 10 mg once daily
drugs.notes: For compelling indications or as a fourth-line agent.
